paper_title: Galois Energy Games: To Solve All Kinds of Quantitative Reachability Problems
statement: Parity Games. An energy parity game [2, 24] is an energy game with a ranking function that assigns each position a natural number (called priority) and has a finite image. Then, infinite plays where the energy level never becomes undefined are won by the attacker if and only if the lowest priority appearing infinitely often is even. A stronger objective for the attacker would be to never visit more than l positions with odd priority before visiting a position with a smaller even priority for a fixed l P N. Abdulla et al. [2] show that deciding games with that stronger objective in some cases is equivalent to deciding energy parity games. Such energy parity games with vector addition only can be formulated as an energy game with safety winning conditions as described by Chatterjee et al. [11] where dimensions corresponding to the odd priorities are added. Whether such a procedure can be applied to other kinds of updates remains an open question.

In both-bounded energy games [18] both players are energybound. This is modeled by assigning two updates to each edge, operating on pairs of current energies – one for the attacker, one for the defender. Considering such games over vectors of naturals, undecidability arises if one player has one-dimensional energies and the other two, so our results cannot be transferred.
